findings.title: Resource leak: opened file not closed
findings.body: The file opened on line 7 is appended to `_open_reports` but never closed, causing a resource leak. The previous implementation used a context manager (`with`) to ensure the file was closed immediately after reading. The new code does not close the file, leaving it open until program termination or garbage collection.
findings.suggestion:
with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as report:
        return report.read()

findings.title: Global mutable list `_open_reports` introduces hidden state
findings.body: The global list `_open_reports` introduces hidden state and mutable global variables, which are discouraged in Python. This pattern can lead to subtle bugs and makes the code harder to reason about. The previous implementation did not require this global state.

findings.title: Unbounded growth of `_open_reports`
findings.body: The list `_open_reports` grows indefinitely as files are opened, as there is no mechanism to remove closed files from the list. This can lead to memory leaks over time, especially in long-running processes. The previous implementation avoided this issue by closing the file immediately.

summary.problem: The change introduces resource leaks and hidden global state, breaking correctness and readability conventions.
summary.done_well: The new code attempts to track opened files, but the implementation introduces more problems than it solves.
